study.question: Does support-aware shrinkage of field/action semantic vectors recover useful behavior evidence that one global normalized vector and exact-match scalars fail to represent?
study.hypothesis: Observed limitation: incumbent source _field_views returns a single 16-dimensional softmax-normalized sum across actions; equality/rank/transition features cannot represent the semantic content of each rare action. Earlier r0003 action pools failed (AUC .6179337371 vs parent .6184566652) despite first512 diagnostics showing pv attention mass .8981 and only mean3.19/1.27/1.99 cart/fav/buy events. This suggests unshrunk sparse-action pools may add noise; dominance alone is not proof. New provisional mechanism: append separate category/brand x four-action value pools shrunk toward an explicit zero-valued unit-mass null observation. With g=sigmoid(inherited field score), N=sum(g*v), M=sum(g), use N/(M+1); unlike N/M this retains confidence from activation mass while bounding its amplitude. Uniform g=.5 isolates generic count shrinkage. Relevance-specific confidence is supported only if learned/null exceeds learned/mean and uniform/null with a positive factorial interaction, improves the full incumbent and repeats. This is a new implementation hypothesis, not a refutation or rediscovery claim about DIN.

nearest_work.difference: Inherit target-conditioned local activation. DIN explicitly retains intensity by abandoning softmax, so intensity itself is established prior work. Here bounded sigmoid gates and a fixed zero-valued unit-mass null shrink each of eight coarse field/action vectors alongside the complete incumbent; no exact DIN reproduction, new priority, or exhaustive nearest-work claim.
README confirms only category/brand/behavior and no item IDs. Use only exposed fields. Publisher paper unavailable; no claim about matching its detailed method.

Earlier semantic action pooling is nearest local failed trajectory, not scalar summaries. It appended action-normalized attention vectors on an earlier parent. Current study preserves full later incumbent, separates fields, uses sigmoid rather than softmax and specifically tests unit-null shrinkage with matched four cells. Changes across lineage are confounds; do not compare r0003 to current candidates as a matched contrast.

inherited_components: Entire r0033-gap_factorized_symmetric implementation including all historical null/positive choices and exact feature order
Category/brand embeddings, action/recency values, blind static context queries and shared relevance scorer
Adam default host optimization and unchanged training loss, data coverage, temporal split and validation scorer
study.proposed_difference: Eight independent semantic value pools indexed field(category,brand), action(pv,cart,fav,buy), embedding coordinate; same field value = field embedding +.5*(action+recency). Validity requires history_mask, positive history field ID, positive corresponding target ID and type1..4. Learned g=sigmoid(score) or uniform g=.5. For each group compute N=sum(g*v), M=sum(g). Mean uses N/M (zero when M=0); null uses N/(M+1). All four tables are evaluated in each cell, one is appended. Groups are independent; target equality is not required. Null token is a fixed zero vector/unit mass, never a new input, parameter or synthetic event in the history. Value dimension16 fixed;128 extra columns =>16384 new dense parameters, expected17164067 total, unchanged17078688 embedding parameters. No sequence sorting, labels, filesystem/network or randomness added.
predictions: Primary: AUC(learned/null)>AUC(learned/mean), AUC(learned/null)>AUC(uniform/null), and AUC(learned/null)>.6209487954658293 incumbent; Logloss and measured cost reported separately.

Predeclared AUC factorial interaction I=[learned_null-learned_mean]-[uniform_null-uniform_mean]>0 if score-derived mass helps beyond generic count shrinkage. Generic uniform-null gains alone support only support shrinkage.

All four share parameter count and initialization; empty/missing/absent groups are exactly zero, finite; mass>=0 and null pool=mean pool*M/(M+1). Uniform mean recovers arithmetic mean and uniform shrink=M/(M+1)=n/(n+2).

Exploratory fixed existing slices: report all host counts/positives/negatives and AUC/Logloss for empty,1-16,17-64,>64 histories and action present/absent, hour and frequency bins. Expect null shrinkage most consequential for sparse action groups; no full-population rare-action causal claim from prefix diagnostics.

Diagnostics test source identities, gate saturation, per-action valid support, learned-vs-uniform mass, null weight, vector norm and checkpoint replacement dependence. Learned/null utility requires trained controls; replacements alone do not establish utility.
falsifiers: If learned/null fails to beat incumbent or learned/mean, the claimed useful correction is unsupported for this implementation; retain result and stop this branch unless diagnostics identify a discriminating fix.
If uniform/null equals or beats learned/null, or I<=0, do not claim relevance-specific confidence. If both means beat null variants, shrinkage is harmful under this recipe.

If sigmoid gates saturate, masses collapse, or candidate invariants fail, separate implementation/optimization failure from a mechanism test. Correct a concrete bug only within remaining resources; record all charged failed attempts.
A single selected validation improvement without paired seeds remains preliminary. Equal parameter counts do not establish equal measured compute or efficiency.
alternative_explanations: Learned scores also affect inherited attention: shared gradients are part of the intervention
Learned sigmoid gates use absolute score offsets; saturation or score rescaling can masquerade as confidence
Null normalization changes feature magnitude and optimization as well as evidence sensitivity
Adaptively searched validation and one seed per screen; no independent mechanism replication
First512 diagnostics describe a selected small prefix, not population slice estimates

A gain from any appended pool may reflect extra classifier capacity or group separation rather than null confidence; three matched added-input controls address but do not eliminate every representation confound
Null pooling may help simply by reducing feature scale and sparse-event gradients, rather than a calibrated notion of confidence
Only 128 recent supplied events and coarse IDs are available; older omitted history, item journeys and real-world causal processes remain unobserved
